newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan deports gate-crashing Afghan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan deports gate-crashing Afghan refugees.

text.p: Some 50 refugee families fleeing new fighting in eastern Afghanistan were deported by Pakistan on Wednesday hours after they forced their way across the border, a Pakistan government official said.

This was the first time Pakistan has expelled Afghan refugees since they started arriving 17 years ago after Marxists seized power in Afghanistan, according to Khyber Agency political agent Javed Iqbal.

The refugee families forced their way across the Torkham border point in the Khyber Pass on Tuesday evening but were stopped about five km (three miles) into Pakistan and were deported before dawn on Wednesday, Iqbal said.
"We have to go by government policy...not to allow fresh refugees and those without valid travel documents," he said.

Pakistan closed its border with Afghanistan last week when the rebel Taleban Islamic militia launched an offensive in eastern Afghanistan seizing two pro-government provinces. But officials say more than 5,000 refugees have arrived via unfrequented routes.
Pakistani authorities said on Tuesday they would set up a new camp outside the northwestern town of Peshawar to house the new Afghan refugees.

A government statement said the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees had agreed to supply tents for the camp at Nasir Bagh and request non-governmental organisations to provide food and other "basic assistance" to the refugees.
Pakistan took in more than three million Afghan refugees during the Soviet occupation of their country in the 1980s and many of them are still living here.
